subject: Food Science
title: The Delaney Clause
description: A 60-second lesson on The Delaney Clause.

hook.text: The Delaney Clause of 1958 banned any food additive shown to cause cancer in animals. Zero tolerance.

buildup.text: Congressman James Delaney pushed the law after learning that some food dyes caused cancer in lab rats.

discovery.text: The clause was absolute—no safe dose. If a substance caused cancer at any dose in any animal, it was banned.

twist.text: Modern science shows dose matters. Substances carcinogenic at massive doses may be safe at tiny exposures.

climax.text: The clause was effectively weakened in 1996 for pesticides, allowing 'negligible risk' standards instead.

punchline.text: Zero risk sounds safe. But zero risk isn't how chemistry works.

quiz.question: What did the Delaney Clause mandate about food additives?
options: Zero tolerance—any additive causing cancer in animals was banned regardless of dose
